children: will report fiscal-first-quarter earnings after Thursday's close, with shares down approximately 7.25% to $351.045 around 11.30 a.m. ET. That puts pressure on the evening's numbers. Investors need evidence that demand for high-capacity hard drives can keep revenue and profits climbing despite the retreat in AI stocks.

Management's previous guidance set revenue at $4.0 billion$4.2 billion and adjusted earnings at $3.85$4.15 per share, with a 55.5% adjusted gross margin at the midpoint. The hurdle could be higher: Barron's reported that analysts expected adjusted earnings of $4.11 per share on roughly $4.1 billion in revenue. Hitting management's $4.00 earnings midpoint would therefore leave profits below that consensus estimate.

The valuation picture adds another challenge: shares stand 340.18% above the $79.75 GF Value estimate, suggesting substantial growth expectations remain baked into the price. That estimate is a valuation reference, not a near-term price target. Still, the gap makes the next outlook crucial. Strong hyperscale demand needs to translate into durable pricing and margins; a solid quarter alone may leave investors wanting more.

title: Western Digital Stocks Sink 7.3% Before AI-Storage Earnings
